none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained optimization of an everywhere Fréchet differentiable function f:E→ℝ; convexity is not required. The derivative satisfies ‖Df(x)−Df(y)‖≤L‖x−y‖. There exists a global lower bound lower with f(x0)−lower≤Δ. All parameters, including E, L>0, Δ≥0, ε>0, and x0, are public; f is the instance.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothNonconvexNonEuclidean.lean: Params; spec.Public, publicInput, Instance, valid, admissible.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns the exact Fréchet derivative Df(x), a continuous linear functional E→ℝ. Exactness holds for every call index and seed by uniqueness of the derivative. No function values or oracle errors are supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothNonconvexNonEuclidean.lean: spec.Query, Reply, and first two conjuncts of admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary complete real normed space with a measurable-space structure, potentially infinite dimensional. No inner product or additional geometric assumption is imposed. Smoothness and stationarity use the operator norm on the dual space E*.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothNonconvexNonEuclidean.lean: Params.normedE, linearE, completeE, measurableE; spec.Reply, admissible, successful.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm_squared
accuracy.details: The output X takes values in E and must satisfy E[‖Df(X)‖²]≤ε², using the continuous-linear-functional operator norm. X must be measurable and its squared derivative norm integrable.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The guarantee is an expectation under the supplied probability measure P. In Convergence, P is the product of the algorithm and oracle seed laws; no deterministic or almost-sure accuracy guarantee is required.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation requires smooth nonconvex stationarity over arbitrary real Banach spaces, with dual-valued derivative access and no additional geometry. This generality extends beyond the usual Euclidean or Hilbert-space benchmark.
